newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai food exporters urge boycott of some EU goods.
newsitem.headline: Thai food exporters urge boycott of some EU goods.

text.p: Thai food exporters on Wednesday sought a boycott of goods from the European Union (EU) after the it ended tariff privileges on three categories of Thai food exports to the bloc.

The Thai Frozen Foods Association urged people not to buy food and beverages imported from the EU, such as liquor and powdered milk, and instead purchase local brands or imports from non-EU countries.

It said the boycott followed the EU decision to end privileges under the Generalised System of Preferences on Thai vegetables and fruits, processed food and beverages and fishery products from January 1.

"Export earnings from these goods exported to the EU amounted to more than 15 billion baht (US$600 million) annually and were expected to rise steadily every year if Thailand had not been removed from...the privileges," the association said.
"The Thai government has requested the EU several times in the past not to increase the tariffs on Thai agricultural products but the EU didn't want to negotiate," it added.
"So it's about time for all of us to unite and avoid buying goods from the EU in order to assist Thai farmers," it said.
The association said it believed the European Union would return to the negotiating table within three months if it found its exports to Thailand were cut because of the boycott.
